source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on the psychiatric unit looks frightened and says, 'I feel like I'm losing control.' What is the nurse's MOST appropriate action?
options: Give the PRN anxiolytic right away
Place the client in seclusion
Take the client to a quiet room and talk
Tell the client to join the group activity
questions.rationale: A quiet setting lowers environmental stimuli, and talking lets the nurse find the cause of the feelings. Medication is used only after noninvasive approaches fail, and seclusion is for clients who are a danger to themselves or others.
explanations: Medication comes after less invasive measures fail.
Seclusion is not warranted for anxiety without danger.
Correct: reduces stimuli and opens communication.
A group setting adds stimulation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 767)
questions.quote: Moving the client to a quiet setting decreases environmental stimuli.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with depression asks how cognitive therapy works. Which explanation by the nurse is accurate?
options: 'It examines how your thoughts affect your feelings and mood.'
'It uncovers memories from your early childhood.'
'It rewards you each time you show a desired behavior.'
'It relies mainly on medicines to correct your mood.'
questions.rationale: Cognitive therapy examines the client's thoughts and feelings about situations and how they keep the difficulties and low mood going, then builds new coping skills.
explanations: Correct: this is the core of cognitive therapy.
This describes psychoanalytic therapy.
This describes behavior modification.
Cognitive therapy is a psychotherapy, not drug treatment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 829)
questions.quote: how these thoughts and feelings contribute to and perpetuate the client’s difficulties and mood.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which outcome is MOST realistic in the care plan of an older client with dementia?
options: The client will be admitted to a nursing home
Staff will perform all of the client's daily care
The client will function as independently as possible
The client will recall the date on every shift
questions.rationale: Every client is encouraged to function at the highest level of independence possible, which supports a sense of control and well-being. Placement and staff-performed care are not client-centered goals.
explanations: Placement is not a client-centered outcome.
This fosters dependence.
Correct: maximal independence is client-centered and realistic.
Expecting full orientation is unrealistic in progressive dementia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1026)
questions.quote: All clients, regardless of age, need to be encouraged to perform at the highest level of independence possible.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: During home visits, the nurse suspects that the wife of a bedridden client is experiencing caregiver strain. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Refer the family to a social worker
Advise placing the client in a facility
Arrange a paid caregiver for the family
Gather data from both the wife and the client
questions.rationale: Before any referral, the nurse assesses the caregiver's stressors and coping abilities by collecting data from both the caregiver and the client.
explanations: Referrals wait until the assessment is complete.
This is premature without assessment.
This is premature without assessment.
Correct: assessment comes first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 935)
questions.quote: The nurse gathers data from the client and the caregiver to determine the caregiver’s stressors and coping abilities

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which activity plan is BEST for a newly admitted client with major depression?
options: Quiet, solitary activities in the room
A structured schedule of simple activities
Letting the client choose whether to join
Competitive team games to lift the mood
questions.rationale: Depressed clients are withdrawn, fatigued, and struggle to concentrate. The plan provides stimulation within a structured environment, using simple tasks the client can complete.
explanations: Solitude supports withdrawal.
Correct: structure plus stimulation.
A depressed client will likely choose not to participate.
Competition can reinforce feelings of worthlessness.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 776)
questions.quote: The plan of care needs to provide stimulation in a structured environment.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is an appropriate maintenance goal for a client being discharged with chronic anxiety?
options: Eliminating all anxiety from daily life
Calling a counselor whenever anxiety starts
Ignoring anxious feelings until they pass
Identifying situations that trigger anxiety
questions.rationale: Recognizing triggers lets the client prepare coping strategies or avoid a specific stimulus. Anxiety cannot be eliminated, and relying on others does not build internal strengths.
explanations: It is impossible to eliminate all anxiety.
This does not develop internal coping.
Ignoring feelings does not resolve anxiety.
Correct: recognizing triggers allows coping.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 796)
questions.quote: Recognizing situations that produce anxiety allows the client to prepare to cope with anxiety or avoid a specific stimulus.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The mother of a teenager with an anxiety disorder asks what changes at home would help. Which advice is BEST?
options: Keep her home from school for a month
Stop her from seeing any friends
Limit coffee, energy drinks, and chocolate
Let her eat whatever calms her down
questions.rationale: Caffeine, chocolate, and alcohol can increase anxiety and should be limited. Isolating the teen from school and peers is unhealthy and unrealistic.
explanations: Prolonged school avoidance is unhealthy.
Restricting all peer contact is unreasonable.
Correct: stimulants can worsen anxiety.
Food choices can worsen symptoms.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 903)
questions.quote: Clients diagnosed with anxiety disorders are advised to limit their intake of caffeine, chocolate, and alcohol

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with bipolar disorder on lithium carbonate has a serum level of 1.6 mEq/L. Which question BEST checks for early toxicity?
options: 'Have you had nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea?'
'Is your vision blurred?'
'Have you had any seizures?'
'Are you passing a lot of urine?'
questions.rationale: The maintenance range is 0.8 to 1.2 mEq/L. Gastrointestinal upset (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) is one of the most common early signs of mild toxicity; blurred vision and seizures occur at higher levels.
explanations: Correct: GI symptoms are early signs of toxicity.
Blurred vision appears at higher levels.
Seizures occur at much higher levels.
Polyuria can occur but is not the key early sign of toxicity.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: One of the most common early signs of lower level lithium toxicity is gastrointestinal (GI) disturbances such as nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client's serum lithium level is 3.9 mEq/L. Which intervention is the PRIORITY?
options: Check visual acuity
Assist with ambulation
Monitor intake and output
Institute seizure precautions
questions.rationale: A level of 3.9 mEq/L is in the toxic range, and seizures can occur at 3.5 mEq/L and above. Seizure precautions come first.
explanations: Not the priority at this level.
Appropriate, but secondary.
Appropriate, but secondary.
Correct: seizures may occur at this level.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 759)
questions.quote: seizures may occur at levels of 3.5 mEq/L (3.5 mmol/L) and higher.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia is pacing, speaking rapidly, and making threatening gestures. What is the nurse's PRIORITY?
options: Ensuring the safety of the client and others
Exploring the client's anger in group therapy
Ignoring the behavior to avoid reinforcing it
Documenting the behavior in detail
questions.rationale: Signs of loss of control make safety for everyone on the unit the immediate priority. Exploring feelings comes later, and ignoring the behavior risks escalation.
explanations: Correct: safety of all clients comes first.
Not appropriate while the client is escalating.
Ignoring it risks violence.
Documentation is not the priority action.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 645)
questions.quote: the nurse’s immediate priority is to ensure safety for all clients.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia has visual hallucinations. Which lobe of the cerebrum is associated with this symptom?
options: Frontal lobe
Temporal lobe
Parietal lobe
Occipital lobe
questions.rationale: The occipital lobe processes vision and is linked to visual hallucinations. The temporal lobe processes hearing and is linked to auditory hallucinations.
explanations: The frontal lobe governs thinking, judgment, and behavior.
The temporal lobe is linked to auditory hallucinations.
The parietal lobe processes touch and sensation.
Correct: the occipital lobe processes vision.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1031)
questions.quote: The occipital lobe is located in the back of the head and is primarily responsible for seeing and receiving information and is responsible for visual hallucinations.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client who attempted suicide is now hallucinating and delusional. Which intervention BEST ensures the client's safety?
options: Check the client's location every 15 minutes
One-to-one observation at all times
Ask the client to report suicidal thoughts
Keep the client in the dayroom with others
questions.rationale: Hallucinations and delusions increase unpredictable behavior, impair judgment, and raise suicide risk, so constant one-to-one supervision is needed.
explanations: Fifteen-minute checks leave gaps in supervision.
Correct: constant observation is required.
A psychotic client cannot be relied on to report.
Being among others is not the same as dedicated observation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 594)
questions.quote: Both of these factors increase the risk of unpredictable behavior, compromised judgment, and the risk of suicide.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Mang Lito, 50, has alcohol use disorder and wants to stay sober. His physician prescribes disulfiram.
questions.stem: Before giving the first dose, which information is MOST important for the nurse to obtain?
options: The time of his last full meal
The time of his last alcoholic drink
His usual sleep pattern
His last bowel movement
questions.rationale: The client must abstain from alcohol for at least 12 hours before the first dose of disulfiram, or a severe reaction can occur.
explanations: Meal timing does not affect safety here.
Correct: alcohol must be avoided for at least 12 hours before the first dose.
Not related to disulfiram safety.
Not related to disulfiram safety.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1796)
questions.quote: Clients must abstain from alcohol intake for at least 12 hours before the initial dose of the medication is administered.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Mang Lito, 50, has alcohol use disorder and wants to stay sober. His physician prescribes disulfiram.
questions.stem: Which statement by Mang Lito shows he understands the teaching about disulfiram?
options: 'One bottle of beer on weekends is still okay.'
'Vinegar dips and sauces are safe to eat.'
'I will check cough syrups and mouthwash for alcohol.'
'Rubbing alcohol on my skin will not matter.'
questions.rationale: Any alcohol can trigger a disulfiram reaction, including hidden sources: vinegar and sauces, cold medicines, mouthwash, and alcohol rubs or aftershave.
explanations: Any alcohol intake causes a reaction.
Vinegars and some sauces contain alcohol.
Correct: hidden alcohol must be avoided.
Skin preparations containing alcohol can also cause a reaction.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1358)
questions.quote: Sources of hidden alcohol include foods (soups, sauces, and vinegars), medicine (cold medicine), mouthwashes, and skin preparations

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client is admitted after an attempted hanging. Which intervention is MOST important for the client's safety?
options: A staff member stays with the client at all times
The client agrees to report suicidal thoughts
The client wears a hospital gown only
The client is placed in seclusion
questions.rationale: Hanging is a serious suicide attempt, so constant observation by a staff member is necessary. The client cannot be relied on to report suicidal thoughts at this stage.
explanations: Correct: constant observation is required.
Self-report is unreliable this early.
Removing clothing alone does not ensure safety.
Seclusion isolates the client without the needed observation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 780)
questions.quote: Constant observation by a staff member is necessary.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A caller tells the crisis hotline nurse that he wants to kill himself and has a loaded gun on the table. What is the BEST action?
options: Ask him to unload the gun and go to the hospital
Tell him to call back after he has calmed down
Keep him on the line while sending help
Ask why he wants to end his life
questions.rationale: In a crisis the nurse takes an authoritative, active role. Keeping the caller on the phone while getting help to him best protects his safety.
explanations: This relies on him to act alone and lacks authoritative action.
Ending the call abandons the client in crisis.
Correct: maintain contact and dispatch help.
Exploring reasons can wait until he is safe.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 781)
questions.quote: Keeping the client on the phone and getting help to the client is the best intervention.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Before discharging a victim of family violence from the emergency room, what is MOST important to include in the plan?
options: Referral to marriage counseling
A safety plan for leaving dangerous situations
A follow-up visit in one month
Advice to avoid provoking the partner
questions.rationale: In the emergency setting, the most important step is helping the victim plan how to get away from harmful situations if they arise.
explanations: Counseling may come later and is not the immediate priority.
Correct: a safety plan protects the victim now.
Follow-up is secondary to immediate safety.
This blames the victim and is inappropriate.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 772)
questions.quote: It is most important to assist victims of abuse with identifying a plan for how to remove self from harmful situations should they arise.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which event is an example of a situational crisis?
options: Retirement from work
Birth of a first child
A strong earthquake
Sudden loss of a job
questions.rationale: A situational crisis comes from an external, often unexpected event such as job loss, divorce, or death of a loved one. Retirement and childbirth are maturational crises; natural disasters are adventitious crises.
explanations: Retirement is a maturational (developmental) crisis.
Childbirth is a maturational crisis.
A natural disaster is an adventitious crisis.
Correct: job loss is an unanticipated external event.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 919)
questions.quote: A situational crisis arises from an external rather than an internal source and often is unanticipated.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client becomes physically aggressive toward staff. Which action BEST protects the milieu while preserving the client's rights?
options: Apply wrist restraints right away
Sedate the client before talking
Lock the client in a room until calm
Try de-escalation and a sitter first
questions.rationale: Alternatives must be exhausted before restraints. If restraint becomes necessary, it requires a prescription and an explanation to the client and family.
explanations: Restraints come only after alternatives fail and need a prescription.
Chemical restraint also requires less restrictive measures first.
Seclusion without a prescription violates rights.
Correct: the least restrictive measures come first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 782)
questions.quote: Before applying restraints, the nurse must exhaust alternative measures to restraints such as a bed alarm, distraction, and a sitter.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client's central venous catheter disconnects from the IV tubing, and the nurse suspects an air embolism. How should the nurse position the client immediately?
options: High Fowler's position
Left side in Trendelenburg
Right side, head elevated
Flat on the back
questions.rationale: Left side-lying in Trendelenburg traps air in the right atrium, away from the pulmonary outflow, where it can be aspirated if needed.
explanations: Head-up positions let air travel toward the brain and lungs.
Correct: traps air in the right atrium.
This elevates the head and does not trap the air.
Supine does not trap the air effectively.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 282)
questions.quote: If the client develops an air embolism, the immediate action is to place the client in Trendelenburg’s position on the left side.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with a suspected neck injury is unresponsive and pulseless. How should the nurse open the airway?
options: Jaw-thrust maneuver
Head-tilt, chin-lift
Recovery position
Neck hyperextension
questions.rationale: The jaw thrust opens the airway without moving the cervical spine and is used until an x-ray confirms the spine is stable.
explanations: Correct: opens the airway while protecting the cervical spine.
Head tilt moves the neck and risks cord damage.
Not a method of opening the airway in a pulseless client.
Hyperextension can worsen a spinal injury.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 312)
questions.quote: The health care team uses the jaw-thrust maneuver to open the airway until a radiograph confirms that the client’s cervical spine is stable

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which findings should the nurse expect in a client developing cardiogenic shock after a myocardial infarction?
options: Warm, flushed skin and bounding pulses
Cool, clammy skin and a weak, thready pulse
Dry, hot skin and slow pulse
Pink skin and rising urine output
questions.rationale: Cardiogenic shock causes a rapid, weak, thready pulse, falling blood pressure and urine output, confusion or agitation, and cool, clammy skin.
explanations: Warm, flushed skin suggests early septic shock.
Correct: classic signs of low cardiac output.
Shock causes tachycardia, not a slow pulse.
Urine output falls in shock.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 340)
questions.quote: increased pulse (weak and thready); decreased blood pressure; decreasing urinary output

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on oxygen by nasal cannula at 6 L/min has these ABGs: pH 7.29, PaCO2 49 mm Hg, PaO2 58 mm Hg, HCO3 18 mEq/L. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: Lowering the oxygen to 2 L/min
Switching to a partial rebreather mask
Intubation and mechanical ventilation
Keeping the oxygen at 6 L/min
questions.rationale: The client has combined respiratory and metabolic acidosis with hypoxemia despite supplemental oxygen. When oxygen cannot maintain acceptable PaO2 and PaCO2, intubation and mechanical ventilation are needed.
explanations: Less oxygen would worsen hypoxemia.
A mask will not correct the ventilatory failure.
Correct: oxygen alone has failed to maintain gas exchange.
The current therapy is already failing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 308)
questions.quote: If respiratory failure occurs and supplemental oxygen cannot maintain acceptable Pao2 and Paco2 levels, endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation are necessary.
